## The trap

When you drive the Tauri desktop on a headless box by spawning a bare
`Xvfb` and screenshotting it (`import -window …`), **every screenshot
comes back uniformly blank white — regardless of what the webview's DOM
actually contains.** It looks exactly like a broken or non-rendering app.
It is not. The DOM is fine; the *pixels* never render.

Why: a plain `Xvfb` is a software framebuffer with **no DRI3 / no GL**.
The tell is in the app log:

```
libEGL warning: DRI3 error: Could not get DRI3 device
```

WebKitGTK's accelerated compositor can't get a GL context, so it never
paints the webview to the framebuffer. The window chrome (titlebar, drawn
by the WM) shows up; the webview content area is blank.

This burned ~hours in the desktop-ipc Phase-4 packaged smoke
(2026-06-01): the "blank window" across every boot was read as a render
failure, when it was purely the GL-less Xvfb. The giveaway was that
**every screenshot was the exact same byte size** — the framebuffer never
changed because nothing ever painted into it.

## Why it's easy to miss

- On a **release** build there's no dev bridge (`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`),
  so a screenshot is your *only* introspection — and it lies (blank).
- On a **debug** build the bridge (`tauri-agent-tools`) reads the **DOM**,
  not pixels, so it works fine GL-less — which is why DOM-level checks pass
  while screenshots look broken. The two disagree, and the screenshot is
  the wrong one.
- `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` / `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` /
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` do **not** fix it here (NVIDIA box; mesa
  software paths don't drive the NVIDIA card).

## The fix — get real GPU GL

Two options:

1. **Run on `:0`** (the real GPU X server): `DISPLAY=:0 …`. Simplest, but
   opens a window on the operator's actual screen (focus-steal).
2. **VirtualGL on an isolated Xvfb** — *recommended* (no focus-steal, real
   GPU). `vglrun` routes GL to the GPU's EGL render node while the app
   displays to the isolated Xvfb.

VirtualGL isn't in Ubuntu apt; install the GitHub release once:

```sh
curl -sSL -o /tmp/vgl.deb \
  https://github.com/VirtualGL/virtualgl/releases/download/3.1.4/virtualgl_3.1.4_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i /tmp/vgl.deb
```

**Always confirm you got the real GPU, not `llvmpipe`/`swrast`:**

```sh
Xvfb :90 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 -nolisten tcp & sleep 2
DISPLAY=:90 vglrun -d egl0 glxinfo | grep -i "OpenGL renderer"
# → OpenGL renderer string: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090/...   ✅
# → ...llvmpipe / swrast                                  ❌ still software
```

Then launch the app **under `vglrun`** so WebKitGTK composites on the GPU:

```sh
( cd papercusp-desktop && DISPLAY=:90 vglrun -d egl0 npm run dev ) &
DISPLAY=:90 import -window root /tmp/shot.png   # now shows REAL content
```

## Gotchas

- Use **`-d egl0`** — the EGL **device index**. Do **not** pass the
  `/dev/dri/renderD128` path: VGL rejects it with `[VGL] ERROR: Invalid EGL
  device`.
- If you see `libEGL ... failed to create dri2 screen` with `-d egl0`, the
  mesa loader is fighting NVIDIA; `-d egl0` already selects the NVIDIA EGL
  device (`EGL_NV_device_cuda` in `eglinfo`), so it still works — the
  warning is noise as long as `glxinfo` reports `NVIDIA`.
- The render node is `/dev/dri/renderD128` (`crw-rw----+ root render`); the
  invoking user must be in the `render` group (or it's ACL-granted).

See the full cookbook in
[testing/agent-e2e §15.4](/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e#154-xvfb--xdotool--ocr-fallback-cookbook).
